facts.statement: No one other than the applicant may alter a written application without the applicant's written consent.
facts.quote: No alteration on any written application for any such policy or contract shall be made by any person other than the applicant without his written consent

items.stem: While processing a life application, a producer notices the applicant left the tobacco-use question blank and wants to fill it in. Under New Jersey law, the producer:
options: Must get the insurer's written approval first
Must get the applicant's written consent first
Must get the beneficiary's written consent first
Must initial the change and then tell the applicant
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:24-3 bars anyone other than the applicant from altering a written application without the applicant's written consent.

facts.statement: The insurer may make insertions for administrative purposes only, marked clearly as not attributable to the applicant.
facts.quote: insertions may be made by the insurer, for administrative purposes only, in such manner as to indicate clearly that such insertions are not to be ascribed to the applicant

items.stem: Which change to a written life application may be made without the applicant's written consent?
options: Producer corrections of spelling errors in answers
Insurer updates to the applicant's medical history
Producer additions of omitted answers from notes
Insurer office codes visibly not the applicant's
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:24-3 allows only insurer insertions for administrative purposes, made so they clearly are not attributed to the applicant. Other alterations need the applicant's written consent.

facts.statement: A false statement in the application bars recovery only if it materially affected acceptance of the risk or the hazard assumed.
facts.quote: may not bar the right to recovery thereunder unless such false statement materially affected either the acceptance of the risk or the hazard assumed by the insurer

items.stem: An applicant overstated his height by one inch. Under the insurer's guidelines, his correct height would have produced the same underwriting decision and premium. He dies within the contestable period. Under New Jersey law, the insurer:
options: May deny, since the policy is still contestable
Must pay, since the misstatement was not material
May reduce the benefit to reflect the correct height
May deny the claim but must refund the premiums
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:24-3 provides that a false statement in the application does not bar recovery unless it materially affected the acceptance of the risk or the hazard assumed. Being within the contestable period does not change that.

facts.statement: An application is admissible as evidence only if a copy was attached to or endorsed on the policy when issued.
facts.quote: No application for any life or health insurance policy or annuity contract shall be admissible in evidence in any action relative to such policy or contract, unless a copy of the application was attached to or endorsed upon the policy or contract when issued.

items.stem: In a lawsuit over a New Jersey life policy, the insurer wants to rely on statements in the application. The application is admissible only if:
options: It was made part of the policy at issue
The applicant signed it in the producer's presence
The insurer kept the original for at least five years
The application form was filed with the commissioner
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:24-3 makes an application inadmissible in any action on the policy unless a copy was attached to or endorsed on the policy when issued.

facts.statement: On written request after reinstatement or renewal, the insurer must provide a copy of the reinstatement or renewal application within 30 days.
facts.quote: the insurer shall, within 30 days after receipt of such request at its home office, deliver or mail to the person making such request a copy of such application

items.stem: After a New Jersey life policy is reinstated, the insured asks in writing for a copy of the reinstatement application. The insurer must deliver or mail it within:
options: 10 days
15 days
30 days
60 days
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:24-3 requires the insurer to deliver or mail a copy of the reinstatement or renewal application within 30 days after receiving a written request at its home office.

facts.statement: A minor at least 15 years old may contract for insurance or annuities on his own life or on someone in whom he has an insurable interest.
facts.quote: Any minor not less than 15 years of age may, notwithstanding such minority, contract for annuities or for insurance

items.stem: Under New Jersey law, a minor may contract for life insurance on his own life beginning at age:
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:24-2 allows any minor not less than 15 years of age to contract for insurance or annuities on his own life, or on another person in whom he has an insurable interest.

facts.statement: A minor 15 or older may give a valid receipt for insurance payments totaling up to $2,000 a year, if no guardian has been appointed.
facts.quote: As to a minor not less than 15 years of age--a payment or payments in aggregate not exceeding $2,000.00 in any 1 calendar year

items.stem: A 16-year-old beneficiary with no appointed guardian may give the insurer a valid receipt for payments totaling up to what amount in a calendar year?
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:24-2 deems a minor 15 or older competent to receive and acknowledge insurance payments of up to $2,000 in any calendar year, if the insurer has no notice of a guardian.

facts.statement: When replacing a policy, the owner should not cancel the old policy until the new one has been received.
facts.quote: If you decide to replace your policy, don't cancel your old policy until you have received the new one.

items.stem: A client has decided to replace an existing life policy with a new one. When should the old policy be canceled?
options: Once the new application is signed
Once the first new premium is paid
Once the insurer orders a medical exam
Once the new policy has been received
items.explanation: Per the NAIC Life Insurance Buyer's Guide, if you decide to replace a policy, do not cancel the old one until you have received the new one.

facts.statement: Replacing a policy can be costly, partly because early premiums went to the insurer's selling and issuing costs, which may be paid again on a new policy.
facts.quote: Much of what you paid in the early years of the policy you have now paid for the company's cost of selling and issuing the policy. You may pay this type of cost again if you buy a new policy.

items.stem: One reason replacing a life policy can be costly is that:
options: The up-front costs of a new contract may be paid all over again
The old policy's death benefit is reduced once a new application is filed
The new policy's premiums are based on the age at which the old one was issued
The new policy cannot name the same beneficiary as the old one
items.explanation: Per the NAIC Life Insurance Buyer's Guide, much of what was paid in the early years of a policy covered the company's cost of selling and issuing it, and a new policy may charge that cost again.

facts.statement: A producer must submit, with the application, a statement signed by the applicant and producer on whether the applicant has existing policies; if the answer is no, the producer's replacement duties are complete.
facts.quote: If the answer is "no," the producer's duties with respect to replacement are complete.

items.stem: A producer takes a life application, and the applicant states in the signed existing-coverage statement that she owns no other life policies or annuities. Under New Jersey's replacement rules, the producer:
options: Still has to read the replacement notice aloud
Has to notify every insurer the applicant has used
Has to leave a policy summary of the new policy
Has completed her replacement duties
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-2.3 requires a statement signed by the applicant and producer on existing coverage. If the answer is no, the producer's duties with respect to replacement are complete.

facts.statement: If the applicant has existing coverage, the producer must present and offer to read the replacement notice no later than when the application is taken.
facts.quote: the producer shall present and offer to read to the applicant, not later than at the time of taking the application, a notice regarding replacements

items.stem: In a New Jersey replacement, when must the producer present the replacement notice to the applicant and offer to read it?
options: Before the policy is delivered
Within 5 business days after the application
At the start of the free look period
No later than when the application is taken
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-2.3 requires the producer to present and offer to read the replacement notice not later than at the time of taking the application.

facts.statement: The replacement notice is signed by both the applicant and the producer and stays with the applicant.
facts.quote: The notice shall be signed by both the applicant and the producer

items.stem: Who must sign the New Jersey replacement notice?
options: Both the applicant and the producer
The applicant alone
The producer alone
The applicant and the existing insurer
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-2.3 requires the replacement notice to be signed by both the applicant and the producer, and it remains with the applicant.

facts.statement: In a replacement, the producer must give the applicant the original or a copy of all sales material when the application is completed.
facts.quote: the producer shall give to the applicant, at the time an application for a new policy or contract is completed, the original or a copy of all sales material

items.stem: A producer used a printed brochure and a printed, personalized illustration while replacing a client's old policy. Under New Jersey rules, when must the client receive the original or a copy of this sales material?
options: When the new policy is delivered
When the application is completed
Within 5 business days after the sale
Only if the client asks for them
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-2.3 requires the producer, in a replacement, to give the applicant the original or a copy of all sales material at the time the application is completed. Electronic material must be printed no later than delivery.

facts.statement: The replacing insurer must notify each affected existing insurer within five business days of receiving a completed application indicating replacement.
facts.quote: Notify any other existing insurer that may be affected by the proposed replacement within five business days of receipt of a completed application indicating replacement

items.stem: After receiving a completed application that involves replacement, a New Jersey replacing insurer must notify the existing insurer within:
options: 3 business days
5 business days
10 calendar days
30 calendar days
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-2.4 requires the replacing insurer to notify any affected existing insurer within five business days of receiving a completed application indicating replacement.

facts.statement: In a replacement, the owner has 30 days from delivery to return the new policy for an unconditional full refund.
facts.quote: notice of the right to return the policy or contract within 30 days of the delivery

items.stem: When a new life policy replaces an existing one in New Jersey, the owner may return the new policy for a full refund within how many days of delivery?
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-2.4 requires the replacing insurer to give notice of the right to return the policy within 30 days of delivery for an unconditional full refund. A non-replacement policy has a 10-day minimum.

facts.statement: When the replacing insurer is the same as or affiliated with the existing insurer, it must credit the time already elapsed under the old policy's incontestability and suicide periods.
facts.quote: the replacing insurer shall allow credit for the period of time that has elapsed under the replaced policy's or contract's incontestability and suicide period

items.stem: A policyowner replaces an 18-month-old policy with a new one from the same insurer, for the same face amount. How do the new policy's contestable and suicide periods work under New Jersey rules?
options: Both start over from the new issue date
They are waived because the insurer is the same
Time already served under the old policy counts toward both
The suicide period restarts, but the contestable period is credited
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-2.4 requires a replacing insurer that is the same as or affiliated with the existing insurer to credit the time elapsed under the replaced policy's incontestability and suicide periods, up to the old face amount.

facts.statement: On receiving a replacement notification, the existing insurer must tell the owner in writing within five business days of the right to receive information on the existing policy's values.
facts.quote: Notify the policy or contract owner in writing within five business days of receipt of a notice referred to in (a)1 above that the policy or contract owner has the right to receive information regarding the existing policy or contract values

items.stem: An insurer receives notice that one of its policies is about to be replaced by another company's policy. Under New Jersey rules, what is this existing insurer required to do?
options: Within five business days, send the replacing insurer the old policy's illustration
Within five business days, tell the owner in writing to keep paying premiums on the old policy
Within thirty days, tell the owner in writing about the 30-day right to return the new policy
Within five business days, tell the owner in writing about a right to see current policy values
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-2.6 requires the existing insurer to notify the owner in writing, within five business days of receiving the replacement notice, of the right to receive information on the existing policy's values, such as an in force illustration.
